question_text: [Machine Learning Foundations & Regularization - Q26] Why does increasing L2 regularization (weight decay) coefficient lambda reduce model variance at the expense of increased bias?

options.text: It forces weights to exact zero, performing aggressive feature selection
It constrains the Euclidean norm of weight vectors, smoothing the decision boundary and penalizing extreme parameter sensitivity
It multiplies the gradient learning rate by lambda
It increases the effective degrees of freedom in non-linear models

answer_explanation: L2 regularization adds a quadratic penalty on weights, pulling parameter values towards zero. This reduces parameter magnitude and restricts model capacity, decreasing variance.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: L2 regularization adds a quadratic penalty on weights, pulling parameter values towards zero. This reduces parameter magnitude and restricts model capacity, decreasing variance.
